newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA STAGGER TO 2-1 WIN OVER ECUADOR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA STAGGER TO 2-1 WIN OVER ECUADOR.

text.p: Argentina staggered to a 2-1 win over Ecuador in a South American World Cup qualifier on Wednesday.

The result, which followed their traumatic 2-1 defeat away to Bolivia earlier this month, put Argentina back on course for a place at next year's tournament but their performance was far from encouraging.
Argentina raced into a two-goal lead in little more than half an hour with goals by Ariel Ortega and Hernan Crespo.

But unsung Ecuador, who have never reached the World Cup finals, battled their way back, reducing the deficit with a second-half goal by Alex Aguinaga and nearly forcing an equaliser late in the game.

The win lifted Argentina back into the qualifying spots, taking them above Bolivia, who were third before Wednesday and did not play, and Ecuador, who had been ahead of them in fourth place on the number of goals scored.
The top four in the nine-team South American group qualify for the tournament in France next year. Argentina have 16 points from ten games and Ecuador 13.
Ecuador, who once lost 12-0 to Argentina, appeared intimidated early on as the home side launched attack after attack.

Ortega, Argentina's top player, provided the opening goal when he beat defender Oswaldo Ibarra to a corner and headed the ball into the net. A quarter of an hour later, Crespo increased the lead, shooting in a rebound after Ibarra had saved his first shot.
Far from building on their lead, Argentina's game became scrappy and disjointed, with only Sebastian Veron in midfield showing any signs of life.
After the wild scenes which marred Argentina's game in Bolivia, when their players fought with police in a ten-minute brawl, the game was extremly tame by the standards of South American qualifiers.
But it came to life in the 67th minute when Aguinaga reduced the deficit with a far post header from a cross by Eduardo Hurtado.

Shortly afterwards, Aguinaga, who outshone his rival number ten Ortega throughout the match, slipped a neat pass to Hurtado in the Argentina penalty area but the lanky striker wasted the chance when he failed to control the ball properly.
Hurtado created another chance for himself shortly afterwards but his shot was well saved by Carlos Roa, the sixth goalkeeper to play for Argentina in the qualifiers.

Coach Daniel Passarella, who is bound to come under more fire after the game, showed his anxiety when he took off striker Claudio Lopez and replaced him with defender Eduardo Berizzo fifteen minutes from time.
Ecuador's chances of reaching the finals could be jeopardised by their poor finishing and bad away form. They have taken only one out of 12 points away from home.

Argentina: 1-Carlos Roa, 2-Roberto Ayala, 6-Pablo Paz, 3- Jose Chamot, 5-Matias Almeyda, 8-Diego Simeone, 11-Sebastian Veron, 20-Sergio Berti (15-Hugo Morales, 80), 10-Ariel Ortega, 7-Claudio Lopez (13-Eduardo Berizzo, 76), 9-Hernan Crespo.

Ecuador 12-Oswaldo Ibarra, 3-Wagner Rivera (17-Juan Carlos Urbano, 79), 2-Raul Noriega, 14-Alberto Montano, 18-Edmundo Mendez, 5-Roberto Blandon, 8-Johnny Carabali, 7-Gilson De Souza, 19-Clever Chala (15-Oswaldo de la Cruz, 64), 10-Alex Aguinaga, 9-Eduardo Hurtado.
